title: Minimizing Hitting Time between Disparate Groups with Shortcut Edges

problem.claim: The paper addresses reducing structural bias or segregation between disparate groups in networks by adding shortcut edges to increase inter-group connectivity.

gap.claim: Existing approaches either lack approximation guarantees or simplify optimization by engineering the objective to satisfy desirable properties.

narrative_sequence.summary: Networks can contain internally cohesive but weakly connected disparate groups, creating structural bias or segregation.
Increasing connectivity between groups may reduce social friction and expose people to diverse viewpoints.
A standard intervention is to add shortcut edges, often realized as content recommendations.
Prior work studies this problem using random walks to model network navigation and connectivity.
Prior methods reportedly lack approximation guarantees or modify the objective to make optimization easier.

unknowns: The proposed method or algorithm is not described.
The meaning and role of hitting time are not specified.
No theoretical guarantees, empirical results, datasets, baselines, or quantitative findings are supplied.
The shortcut-edge budget, constraints, and optimization objective are unspecified.
